title: Lala Lajpat Rai Hall of Residence
text:
Lala Lajpat Rai Hall of Residence, also known as LLR Hall is one of the halls of residence for male undergraduate students.

Photocopy

History
The hall was founded on March 18, 1967, and the name was given in honour of the great freedom fighter and leader of Indian Independence Movement, Lala Lajpat Rai.

Infrastructure
The hall has been divided into 4 blocks namely A1, A, B and C. Each of the blocks has two floors above the ground floor. There are 24 wings in the hall (6 in A1 and A blocks & 18 in B and C blocks). The mess and common room are adjacent to the A block and are near the entrance gate. There is one more entrance to the hall apart from the main gate, which is mostly locked and is opened in special occasions. It opens right in the cycle shed of the hall. There was a shed in the back side of the hall which was called as "D-block" but then it was run over by a wall due to some reasons.The hall also provides several recreational and activity facilities for residents. There are four hanging rooms located at C315, C329, B215, and B229. A sports room is available at C142, and the gymnasium is located at A301.

For outdoor sports, the hall has a football ground situated in front of the hall office, a hockey ground between the A ground and B ground, and a badminton court located between the hall mess and the middle of B ground. A cricket ground is also available to the east of the C ground.
center|
center|
center|
Indoor recreational facilities include a table tennis (TT) table, a pool table, and a music room for residents interested in musical activities.
